Theorem
[Circle Classification Theorem]

↗ def:rigid-motion

1. ch1:1.3

Two Euclidean circles are congruent if and only if their radii are equal.
Proof

↗ def:rigid-motion \sketch A circle of radius $R\geq 0$ has diameter $2R$: antipodal points realize this distance, while the triangle inequality bounds every pair of points by $2R$. A rigid motion preserves diameters, so congruent circles have equal radii. If the radii agree, translation by the difference of the centers maps one circle onto the other and is a rigid motion.

□
